title: ZPC cloud identities: classification, power score and attributes

prose.text: The number of identity sources differs between pages {{divergence:identity-sources}}. {{gap:power-score-floor}} {{gap:service-status}}

entitlement-mapping.statement: ZPC scans the cloud deployment for identity metadata and creates a cloud infrastructure entitlement mapping across the permissions and access granted in the public cloud.

quotes: ZPC scans your cloud deployment for identity metadata and creates a cloud infrastructure entitlement mapping across all the permissions and access granted in the public cloud.

human-vs-non-human.statement: ZPC classifies identities as Human (employees and third-party vendors) or Non-Human (service-level needs such as service accounts, virtual machines or lambda functions).

quotes: Human: Identities created for your organization employees and third-party vendors to access your cloud deployment resources.
Non-Human: Identities created to accommodate service-level needs, such as service accounts, virtual machines, or lambda functions.

aws-classification.statement: For AWS, ZPC classifies Instance Profile, Auto Scaling Group and Lambda Function identities as non-human, and Public Account, Canonical User, Federated, Root Account, IAM User and User identities as human.

quotes: | AWS | Non-Human | Instance Profile |
| AWS | Non-Human | Auto Scaling Group |
| AWS | Non-Human | Lambda Function |
| AWS | Human | Public Account |
| AWS | Human | Canonical User |
| AWS | Human | Federated |
| AWS | Human | Root Account |
| AWS | Human | IAM User |
| AWS | Human | User |

azure-classification.statement: For Azure, ZPC classifies Service Principal, Microsoft Apps, Virtual Machine and Managed Identities as non-human, and Microsoft Entra users and Public Account as human.

quotes: | Azure | Non-Human | Service Principal |
| Azure | Non-Human | Microsoft Apps |
| Azure | Non-Human | Virtual Machine |
| Azure | Non-Human | Managed Identities |
| Azure | Human | Other Microsoft Entra (formerly Azure AD) users |
| Azure | Human | Public Account |

gcp-classification.statement: For GCP, ZPC classifies Service Account, Compute Instance, Cloud Function, Group and Domain as non-human, and Public Account and G Suite User as human.

quotes: | GCP | Non-Human | Service Account |
| GCP | Non-Human | Compute Instance |
| GCP | Non-Human | Cloud Function |
| GCP | Non-Human | Group |
| GCP | Non-Human | Domain |
| GCP | Human | Public Account |
| GCP | Human | G Suite User |

power-score.statement: The Viewing Cloud Identity Details page says the power score is a number between 0–100 that ZPC determines from the entitlements an identity holds, and that identities scoring more than 80 are also assigned power categories.

quotes: Power score which is a number between 0–100 determined by ZPC based on the entitlements the identity holds.
Identities that possess more than 80 in power score are also assigned power categories.

power-categories.statement: The power categories ZPC assigns are Data Admin, Storage Admin, Compute Admin, IAM Admin, Security Admin, Infrastructure Admin, CICD Admin, Secret Admin, AI Admin, Log Admin, Application Admin and Cost Admin.

quotes: Data Admin Storage Admin Compute Admin IAM Admin Security Admin Infrastructure Admin CICD Admin Secret Admin AI Admin Log Admin Application Admin Cost Admin

identity-source.statement: The About Cloud Identities page says ZPC categorizes human identities into two sources: local identities as users manually created in a cloud service provider, whose permissions must be manually revoked across all services to remove them, and external identities as authorized users who are not local (for example contractors and federated identities).

quotes: ZPC categorizes human identities into the following two sources:
Local: Users manually created in a cloud service provider. To remove a local user from your organization, you need to manually revoke permissions across all services the user was authorized to use.
External: Users which you have authorized to use your cloud service provider but are not local users (e.g., contractors, federated identities).

mfa-attribute-scope.statement: The Has MFA attribute is offered for AWS and Azure, and cloud service providers supply it only for local identities.

quotes: | Has MFA | AWS, Azure | Identities with multi-factor authentication enabled or not. Cloud service providers offer this information only for local identities. |

aws-auth-attributes.statement: Has Password, Has Access Keys and Has Certificate are AWS-only identity attributes.

quotes: | Has Password | AWS | Identity with password-based authentication. |
| Has Access Keys | AWS | Identity with access key-based authentication. |
| Has Certificate | AWS | Identity with certificate-based authentication. |

azure-attributes.statement: Object ID and User Type are Azure-only identity attributes, with User Type defined by Azure as Guest or Member.

quotes: | Object ID | Azure | Unique Azure identifier for an identity. |
| User Type | Azure | Identity type as defined by Azure as Guest or Member. |

created-on-scope.statement: Created On is available for AWS, Azure and GCP identities, and only for local identities.

quotes: | Created On | AWS, Azure, GCP | Time stamp of when the identity was created on the cloud service provider. This is available only for local identities. |

authentication-tab-aws.statement: The Authentication tab offers password, access key and certificate information for all AWS local identities, and ZPC only displays authentication information for AWS local identities.

quotes: The authentication tab offers authentication information on passwords, access keys, and certificates for all AWS local identities.
ZPC only displays authentication information for AWS local identities.

access-key-fields.statement: For an access key the Authentication tab shows the region and the service in which it was last used.

quotes: Last Used Region: View the region the access key was last used in.
Last Used Service: View the service the access key was last used to authenticate.

identity-export-xlsx.statement: Cloud identities can be exported as a .xlsx file.

quotes: Export cloud identities as a .xlsx file.

identity-alerts-tab.statement: The identity Alerts tab shows alert status as Open, Closed or Resolved and Risk Level as Critical, High, Medium or Low, with Alert Age counted in days from the last time the status was set to Open.

quotes: On the Alerts tab, you can do the following:
Status: The status (Open, Closed, or Resolved) of the alert.
Alert Age: The age of the alert (in days) from the last time the Alert Status was set to Open.
Risk Level: The severity level (Critical, High, Medium, or Low) of the policy violation.

power-score-floor.title: Whether the lowest power score is 0 or 1
power-score-floor.detail: The identity details page and the About Cloud Identities page give the power score as a number between 0–100, while the investigation predicate returns a value between 1-100 (zpc.investigation:power-predicates) and the alert attribute sample is 1–100 (zpc.alerts:attr-identity-power). No captured page says whether a score of 0 occurs.

service-status.title: Whether the ZPC features these pages describe are still available
service-status.detail: portfolio.cloud-protection records ZPC end of life as planned for March 15, 2026 (portfolio.cloud-protection:zpc-eos-eol). None of the captured identity pages says whether it describes a service still available, so none of the identity facts here is claimed as current.

identity-sources.summary: ZPC pages disagree on how many identity sources there are: About Cloud Identities lists two for human identities (Local and External, federated being an example of External), while the Cloud Identities Dashboard lists three (Local, External and Federated) and the investigation results describe Source as federated, local or external.

positions.says: Two sources for human identities, Local and External, with federated identities an example of External.

quotes: ZPC categorizes human identities into the following two sources:
External: Users which you have authorized to use your cloud service provider but are not local users (e.g., contractors, federated identities).
Source: View whether the identity is local or external.

positions.says: Three sources, with Federated separate from Local and External.

quotes: ZPC categorizes identities into the following sources:

Federated: Users that are defined on your user directory such as Okta, and are authorized to use cloud service providers. When you remove a federated user from your organization, they lose all roles and permissions.

positions.says: The Source column in investigation results is federated, local or external.

quotes: Source: View whether the identity is federated, local, or external.

identity-sources.impact: Which grouping ZPC uses, and whether federated identities are a source of their own, is not settled by the pages; the Source column of the Cloud Identities page is described as local or external only.
